findings.reason: without a named minimum target set, or a failure on any exclusion, a node satisfies both the 1e-10 claim and the sheet-route decision by measuring only the far targets that are easy for every route.
findings.text: the reference integral's exclusion clause ("a target that does not reach this is reported and left out, never compared against") puts no cap on how many targets may be excluded and requires no minimum surviving set, while §1 lines 98–101 record that this quadrature is near-singular for sliver cells and reads 4e-5 — so exactly the near targets §2 exists to certify (those at half a cell width) can be dropped and done-when (2)'s 1e-10 claim still reads as met

findings.reason: on the plan's own error model the crossing sits near ε ≈ 5 µm, so a sweep of 1e-2→1e-5 or 1e-3→1e-6 brackets it at one end or misses it entirely, and the sheet-route decision would be taken on a curve that never turns over.
findings.text: done-when (1) requires only that the strip's error "is reported over three decades of ε" — the verb is reporting, so nothing in the clause can fail — and it fixes neither the range's endpoints nor a requirement that the crossing of the ε² model error with the rounding/ε cancellation lies inside the sweep, which is the one number the section is written to find ("measure first where the two cross", line 191)

findings.reason: this is the only quantitative pass condition on the node's primary comparison, and as written it either hides a 1e-11 wiring defect on the strip branch or has no defined value on the Part II branch, so the check cannot tell a correct device build from a wrong one.
findings.text: §3's done-when (1) sets the device-versus-host agreement tolerance to "the strip's cancellation floor, near 1e-11 relative, not a tighter figure neither route can hold", but that floor is the strip's *model* error against the exact sheet (§2 lines 190–191), not the disagreement between two implementations of the same kernel: on the strip branch both sides evaluate the same polygon closed form and should agree at round-off, so 1e-11 is about five decades looser than the comparison can hold; on the Part II branch, which §2 explicitly leaves open, there is no strip and no cancellation floor, so the tolerance names nothing the sheet-route decision will record
